jp: 上司[じょうし]{は|wa-topic}新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]{に対[たい]して/に|nitaishite}とても厳[きび]しいです。
en: The boss is very strict towards new employees.
why: に対して marks the person toward whom an attitude is directed.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}仕事[しごと]{に対[たい]して/に|nitaishite}とても真面目[まじめ]です。
en: My older brother is very serious about his work.
why: に対して marks the thing toward which a person's attitude is directed.

jp: 今年[ことし]{は|wa-topic}男子[だんし]{が/は|ga-subject}多[おお]い{の|no-nominalizer}{に対[たい]して|nitaishite}、去年[きょねん]{は|wa-contrast}女子[じょし]{が/は|ga-subject}多[おお]かったです。
en: This year there are many boys, whereas last year there were many girls.
why: Between two contrasting clauses, に対して means 'whereas'.

jp: お客[きゃく]さん{に対[たい]して/に|nitaishite}失礼[しつれい]な言[い]い方[かた]{を|o-object}してはいけません。
en: You must not speak rudely to customers.
why: に対して marks the person at whom the behavior is directed.

jp: 学生[がくせい]{は|wa-topic}先生[せんせい]{に対[たい]して/に|nitaishite}敬語[けいご]{を|o-object}使[つか]います。
en: Students use honorific language towards their teachers.
why: に対して marks the person toward whom the polite speech is directed.
